primitives.note: Basic attacks alternate Left Punch / Right Punch; the Right Punch is effectively every 2nd basic attack
Right Punch deals bonus physical damage (base by level + 55% bonus AD) on top of the normal attack
Right Punch does not scale with bonus attack speed; its windup is instead fixed as a fraction (12.5%) of Left Punch's windup, still receptive to AS buffs not already active on the prior Left Punch
Knuckle Down resets Sett's basic attack timer and forces the next two attacks to be Left Punch then Right Punch, resetting the Pit Grit alternation state
Knuckle Down arms Sett's next two basic attacks with bonus physical damage based on target's max health
Q's empowered-attack damage and R's slam damage both scale with a percent of the target's max/bonus health
Grit is a stored resource (capped at 50% max HP, decays 30%/s after 4s) that Haymaker fully consumes on cast; its cost is 100% of current Grit
Passive converts post-mitigation damage taken 1:1 into stored Grit; Haymaker converts expended Grit into both a shield and bonus outgoing damage
Each ability deals its damage after a fixed cast time, on cooldown

Haymaker's damage type (true vs physical) depends on whether the target overlaps the inner rectangle vs the trapezoid/circle hitbox; The Show Stopper's damage depends on whether the target is within the 125-unit epicenter or is hit by the falling-off shockwave

needsBespoke.why: The primitives above (nth-hit-or-cast + onhit-rider + attack-speed-interaction for the passive, attack-reset + empowered-attack + conditional-damage for Q, resource-budget + stat-conversion for W, plain-cast + positional-assumption for W/R, conditional-damage for R) together express the kit's mechanics. The main wrinkle - that in a dummy fight where the target never damages Sett, W's Grit income is naturally zero via the stat-conversion/resource-budget primitives rather than needing special-cased logic - is a parameter question (see unsettled), not a modeling gap.

unsettled.question: In the dummy damage fight, does Haymaker's target (the single dummy) take the true damage from the inner rectangle, the physical damage from the trapezoid/circle aoe, or could it receive both simultaneously since the hitboxes are separate and can overlap?
options: Assume the dummy is always in the true-damage line (true damage only)
Assume the dummy is only in the outer aoe (physical damage only)
Assume the dummy overlaps both hitboxes and takes both instances of damage
quotes: those hit in a line in the middle are dealt {{ccs|{{sti|{{as|true damage}}}}|true}} instead.
Enemies are hit by ''Haymaker'' only when their hitbox overlaps with both of those areas.

unsettled.question: Since the target dummy never damages Sett, does the simulated fight credit Sett with any Grit for Haymaker's expended-Grit damage/shield term (e.g., an assumed pre-fight cap, or self-inflicted sources), or should Grit be treated as 0 throughout, leaving Haymaker at its flat base damage only?
options: Grit stays at 0 (no incoming damage source in a one-sided dummy fight)
Assume Sett opens the fight at or near the 50% max-HP Grit cap and casts Haymaker immediately
Assume some intermediate/decayed Grit value is available on each cast
quotes: up to a cap of {{as|50% of his '''maximum''' health}}

unsettled.question: The Show Stopper's health-scaling term is described on the wiki as a percent of the target's 'bonus' health, but the bin variable name (SettR.MaxHealthDamage, feeding SettR#MaxHealthDamageCalc) reads as target max health with no separate bonus-health-only row. Which is the live behavior?
options: Use target's bonus (non-base) health per the wiki text
Use target's total max health per the bin's calculation naming

unsettled.question: For The Show Stopper's shockwave, is the dummy assumed to be the primary/suppressed target standing within the 125-unit epicenter (full damage), or elsewhere in the shockwave radius (reduced damage, up to 75% per wiki text vs a 0.5 multiplier implied by the bin's CraterEdgeDamageReduction)?
options: Dummy (the suppressed target) always lands in the epicenter and takes full damage
Dummy could be treated as an 'edge' hit with a 75% reduction per the wiki's arithmetic
Dummy is an edge hit with a 50% reduction per the bin's CraterEdgeDamageReduction=0.5
quotes: other enemies hit by the shockwave take {{as|physical damage}} that is reduced by up to 75% based on proximity.

unsettled.question: The Right Punch's bonus physical damage base value comes from an unresolved ByCharLevelFormulaCalculationPart in the bin; the wiki's stated pp-formula (linear 5 to 90 across levels 1-20) is used as a stand-in. Is this the actual live per-level progression?
options: Trust the wiki's linear 5-to-90 formula as exact
Treat the exact by-level base as unverified pending the resolved bin formula

proposal: Open with R (The Show Stopper) on the dummy if it is off cooldown, since it is Sett's single biggest burst hit and a 15s fight likely only fits one cast.
Immediately follow with Q (Knuckle Down) to guarantee a Left Punch then Right Punch with bonus max-health-based damage and to reset the attack timer.
Continue basic-attacking on-cooldown throughout, letting Left/Right Punch alternate naturally between other ability casts.
Cast E (Facebreaker) on cooldown for its flat physical AoE hit whenever it is up.
Cast W (Haymaker) on cooldown as well, even though expended Grit is likely near zero absent incoming damage, for its flat base damage component.
Re-cast Q every time it comes off cooldown (9s down to 5s), since its empowered attacks are cheap, resource-free, and scale with the dummy's max health.
Repeat the Q/E/W/auto-attack loop for the remainder of the 15 seconds; do not expect a second R cast given its 80-120s cooldown.
questions: Does the simulator grant Sett any starting or accruing Grit in a one-sided dummy fight, or is Haymaker's Grit-based damage/shield term always effectively zero?

Is R assumed available at the start of the fight (i.e., is the simulated encounter timed to line up with R's cooldown), or should the rotation assume R is unavailable and plan around Q/W/E/autos only?
Where is the dummy assumed to stand relative to Sett for Haymaker's true-damage line versus its outer physical aoe, and relative to Show Stopper's epicenter versus shockwave edge?
Does the simulator track and enforce the Left/Right Punch alternation state (and its 2-second reset window) between ability casts, or does every basic attack default to a fixed damage value?
